title: Baked Beef Empanadas with Potato and Peppers
summary: Golden, crimped baked empanadas with a buttery pastry and a savoury filling of beef, sweet peppers and tender potato seasoned with cumin and paprika.

ingredients.item: plain flour, plus extra for rolling
fine sea salt or table salt
ice-cold water, plus 1-2 tbsp if needed
large egg, beaten with 1 tbsp water, for glazing
green pepper, cut into 5 mm dice
red pepper, cut into 5 mm dice
fine sea salt or table salt
small potato, peeled and cut into 1 cm cubes

steps.title: Dough
steps.text: Pulse the flour, salt and cold butter in a food processor until the mixture looks like coarse breadcrumbs. Beat the egg with the water, add it and pulse just until the dough clumps, adding 1-2 tbsp more water only if it stays dry. Press into a flat disc, wrap and chill for at least 30 minutes; cold butter and rested gluten make a flaky, easy-to-roll pastry.

steps.title: Base
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat, add the tomato paste and stir for 2 minutes, until it turns brick red. Frying the paste caramelises its sugars and deepens the flavour.

steps.title: Vegetables
steps.text: Add the onion, both peppers, garlic, cumin, paprika, salt and pepper and cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until softened. Stir in the potato and cook for 8-10 minutes more, stirring often, until it is tender at the edges; small cubes cook through fast and keep their shape.

steps.title: Beef
steps.text: Raise the heat to medium-high, add the beef and cook for 6-8 minutes, breaking it up, until browned and it reads 71 °C. Pour in the water and simmer for 2-3 minutes, until the filling is moist but not wet, so the pastry stays crisp.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Spread the filling on a plate and chill for at least 20 minutes, until cold. Warm filling melts the butter in the dough and makes it tear.

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: Heat the oven to 200 °C (180 °C fan) and line 2 trays with baking paper.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Roll the dough on a floured surface to 2-3 mm thick and cut out 12 cm rounds, rerolling the scraps once, to make 12. Spoon about 2 tbsp filling onto one half of each round, brush the edge with water, fold over into a half-moon and press out the air as you seal. Crimp by folding the edge over itself in small pleats, or press it with a fork; a tight seal stops the filling bursting out.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Set the empanadas on the trays, brush with the egg glaze and bake for 20-25 minutes, swapping the trays halfway, until deep golden. Cool for 10 minutes on a rack so the filling settles before serving.

tips: Overfilling is the most common mistake: the seams split in the oven. Two tablespoons is plenty.
Keep the dough cold; if it softens while you shape, chill the rounds for 10 minutes.
Cut the potato small so it cooks through in the pan.
Shaped, unbaked empanadas freeze well; bake from frozen, adding 5-8 minutes.
storage: Keep in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat at 180 °C for 10-12 minutes, until piping hot (74 °C). Freeze baked or unbaked for up to 2 months. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
